messages:
maya: Heads up 1: per-model unit cost card for model-abc is showing ~30% lower cost across the afternoon, but logs show a bunch of longer-tail latencies. Suspect mismatch between billing SKU and runtime variant. Anyone digging in? :mag:
rafi: Interesting. Which runtime variant are you seeing in traces? Quantized vs fp16?
maya: Traces show runtime_variant=quant-4bit at 15:12 but econ card lists model_sku=model-abc-v1.fp16 in the breakdown.
jon: That screams late-binding routing where pricing metadata wasn't updated for fallback chains. We recently added variant demux in router v3.2.
maya: Query I ran to compare:
```
SELECT invocation_id, runtime_variant, billed_sku, latency_ms
FROM invocations
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-22T15:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-22T16:00:00Z'
AND model='model-abc'
LIMIT 50;
```
maya: ~40% of invocations had runtime_variant=quant-4bit but billed_sku=model-abc-v1.fp16.
kim: Oof. So customers got cheaper runtime but paid for fp16? Or the dashboard is showing cheaper cost because we priced quant lower but invoicing used fp16? Which direction is the mismatch?
rafi: Quick check: price_table shows quant-4bit = $0.0009/token, fp16 = $0.0015/token. The econ card is low -> suggests dashboard used quant prices, but billing ledger used fp16 -> bad.
billing-bot: [LEDGER] batch-bill-20260322 processed at 2026-03-22T17:00:00Z for tenant-C.ledger_id=led-88aa
jon: If billing ledger consumed billed_sku from the router's old header path, and the console econ aggregation consumed runtime_variant from the runtime trace, they'd diverge. Need to find where we normalize sku vs runtime_variant.
maya: Grepped the router logs: header X-Model-SKU set to model-abc-v1.fp16 at 15:10 for a fraction of requests, then later router attached runtime_variant=quant-4bit after late-binding. Looks like billing consumers read header earlier in the pipeline.
kim: Mitigation: add a canonical sku emitted by the runtime sidecar into the request trace that both billing and econ reads from. Short-term: reconcile dashboard to ledger for affected window and add a reconciliation flag in UI.
rafi: Also let's add a sanity check query into the nightly billing job: if billed_sku != runtime_variant for >0.5% of tokens, fail the job and alert. We should not let divergent pricing slip through.
jon: Agreed. I'll open two PRs: one to emit runtime_canonical_sku in traces (router + runtime) and one to gate batch-bill with the sanity check.
billing-bot: [ALERT] batch-bill-20260322 reconciler: discrepancy detected for tenant-C: 12.3% tokens billed as fp16 while runtime reported quant-4bit.
maya: For transparency I'll add a note to the econ dash: "Cost preview may diverge from issued invoice during routing transitions; contact billing@redwood if you see >5% delta."
kim: UX: make the per-model card show "billing_consistency": OK / WARN / FAIL with hover explanation + link to ledger diff. Product will appreciate that.
rafi: Quick forensics: which commits touched router v3.2? I see PR #4999 merged yesterday that added late-binding header reorder. Tagging @jon for rollback risk.
jon: I'll revert the header reorder change and replace with emitting the canonical sku instead. Revert PR #4999 -> will coordinate with eng-oncall.
maya: Thanks. For now I'll run a ledger vs econ diff for the last 24h and post numbers.
billing-bot: [INFO] ledger-econ-diff job started job_id=lediff-20260322-01
maya: Update: lediff shows tenant-C invoice reported $12,450 while econ preview avg was $9,100 for same window. That's ~36% delta.
rafi: Yikes. We'll need to credit affected tenants or at least apply adjustments. I'll open a billing request ticket and loop sales + support.
jon: Revert in flight, deploying in 5m. I'll post the deploy id and link to rollback notes.
billing-bot: [INFO] revert-pr-4999 deployment started at 2026-03-22T18:02:00Z deploy_id=dep-7801
maya: Appreciate the quick response. After revert and canonical-sku emission we should run a reconciliation and backfill any missing billing tags for the hour window.
rafi: Putting together runbook: (1) revert PR; (2) emit canonical sku; (3) nightly gate for discrepancy; (4) UI flag + hover; (5) reconcile invoices and notify customers. Assigning owners: jon=router revert + trace emit, kim=UI flag, maya=reconciliation/backfill, rafi=billing gate + credits.
jon: On it. Will follow up with links to PRs and postmortem.
maya: Thanks team. Posting summary to #product and pinging support for customer comms.
